# MOJO RISC-V machine code analysis project 
Small tinkering project to analyze the RISC-V machine code generated by the MOJO language, and to look at how it changes when leveraging MOJO's metaprogramming features.

Companion repository to my blog post on the topic (WIP).

Rough workflow notes can be found in `NOTES.md`. 

*NOTE*: MOJO does not yet have a RISC-V runtime, so the machine code generated by the compiler is not actually executable. This project is purely for analysis and exploration purposes, and focused on the machine code generated by the MOJO compiler, rather than on running the code on actual hardware. This sucks a bit, but it's still interesting to see how the machine code changes when leveraging MOJO's metaprogramming features, and to get a sense of how the MOJO compiler generates machine code in general. It'll also give us a chance to get more familiar with the RISC-V instruction set.
